title: Discrete derivative through a bit flip
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $i$ be a coordinate, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. If $x^i$ denotes the point obtained by flipping coordinate $i$ of $x$, then $D_i f(x)=\frac{f(x)-f(x^i)}{2}\,\sigma(x_i)$, where $D_i f(x)=\frac{f(x_{i\leftarrow0})-f(x_{i\leftarrow1})}{2}$ and $\sigma$ is the sign encoding of a bit.
hypotheses_covered: $i$ is a coordinate in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ (equivalently, an element of $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$)
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. For a real cube function $h$, write $D_i h(x)=\tfrac12(h(x_{i\leftarrow0})-h(x_{i\leftarrow1}))$, where $x_{i\leftarrow b}$ replaces bit $i$ by $b$. For every coordinate $i$ and point $x$, $D_i h(x)=\tfrac12(h(x)-h(x^{\{i\}}))(-1)^{x_i}$, where $x^{\{i\}}$ flips bit $i$.
